title: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
gist: PyTorch's open-source GreenLight now lets an AI reviewer approve PRs from PyTorch maintainers, rebuilding Meta's internal RADAR (Risk Aware Diff Auto Review) system, which auto-lands low-risk diffs behind hard safety checks, a percentile Diff Risk Score and an LLM reviewer. The article frames this alongside OpenAI, Anthropic and Sonar as an industry move to automate code approval through 'scoped trust', driven by AI-generated code outpacing human review. (Note: the source URL slug references Uber agent spend, but the text is entirely about RADAR/GreenLight.)

insights.claim: Meta's RADAR paper reports significant lines of code per human-landed diff rose 105.9% year over year and diffs per developer per month rose 51%, with Meta attributing more than 80% of the increase to agentic AI assistance.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Hard evidence that AI coding agents are materially inflating code output at a hyperscaler, shifting the bottleneck to review/verification tooling.
insights.quote: Significant lines of code per human-landed diff rose 105.9% year over year
insights.locator: RADAR stands for Risk Aware Diff Auto Review

insights.claim: At Meta, code review has not kept pace with AI-driven code volume, and the share of diffs reviewed within 24 hours is dropping.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Review capacity is the new constraint; tools that automate verification/approval address a growing pain point.

insights.claim: Sonar's developer survey of more than 1,000 respondents found 76% generate AI code faster than they can verify it and only 39% always check it before committing.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Quantifies a verification gap that underpins demand for code-quality and automated-review vendors like Sonar.

insights.claim: Meta's RADAR routes diffs by author and source: deterministic codemods are approved via blanket policy, while AI-generated codemods and automated runbooks pass safety checks, a Diff Risk Score and an LLM reviewer, with any failure sending the diff to a human.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: A reusable template for risk-tiered automation of code approval.
insights.locator: RADAR sorts each diff by author and source

insights.claim: RADAR's hard limits exclude open-source, SOX-scoped and extra-review code entirely; runbooks need a clean 60-day record with zero production incidents and low revert/rejection rates, and are capped at up to 2,000 diffs per day.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Shows compliance-scoped code stays human-reviewed even at aggressive adopters; auditors and regulated firms will look to such boundaries.
insights.locator: The safety checks are hard limits

insights.claim: RADAR's Diff Risk Score acts as a percentile gate: allowlisted runbooks may land diffs up to the 50th risk percentile, other AI/bot sources up to the 20th, and human-authored diffs default to the 5th, tunable per organization.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Calibrated, source-dependent risk thresholds are the practical mechanism for trusting automation.
insights.locator: The Diff Risk Score works as a percentile gate

insights.claim: RADAR's final review agent auto-accepts only when it scores confidence of at least 8 out of 10 and classifies all changes into safe categories such as dead-code removal, behavior-preserving refactors, logging additions and new tests; approved bot diffs then wait in a landing queue (24 hours in the paper's diagram) during which a human can still reject.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Conservative LLM gating plus delay windows is how hyperscalers de-risk autonomous code landing.
insights.quote: ACR requires a confidence score of at least 8 out of 10
insights.locator: The last gate is the RADAR Review Agent

insights.claim: PyTorch's GreenLight restricts real AI approvals to authors named in PyTorch's merge rules who already have approval rights on the changed files; all other PRs are reviewed in shadow mode and never become approvals, following Edward Yang's rule that RADAR is predicated on author trust.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Open-source adoption makes auto-approval patterns more mainstream and inspectable beyond Meta.
insights.quote: RADAR is predicated on trust of the author
insights.locator: PyTorch said in May that it would rebuild RADAR

insights.claim: GreenLight scans every five minutes, approves and labels PRs on a land verdict, withdraws any prior approval on a no-land verdict, and permanently drops reverted PRs from every path.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Revert feedback loops are a core safety mechanism in automated approval systems.
insights.quote: a reverted PR is dropped from every path, permanently.
insights.locator: A scan runs every five minutes

insights.claim: OpenAI's Brian Yang said at QCon San Francisco 2026 that ChatGPT Ads, built with Codex since November 2025, has zero human-written production code; everyday changes auto-approve after required checks, critical changes need sandbox validation against copied production traffic plus a human decision, and the target is at least 90% auto-approval for routine PRs.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: A production product built entirely by agents is a strong signal for agentic coding adoption and for demand for sandbox/traffic-replay validation.
insights.quote: the codebase has zero human-written production code

insights.claim: OpenAI's team tunes its automated reviewer weekly against history: when too many bad PRs open they fix the agent, and when bad PRs keep merging they fix the checker.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Treating reviewer calibration as a continuous ops loop is a transferable practice.
insights.locator: The team tunes its automated reviewer every week

insights.claim: Sonar's Manish Kapur frames approval as part of an 'agentic software factory' in which the factory knows which changes can pass on automated evidence and which need a human decision.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Sonar is positioning code-quality tooling as the evidence layer for agentic pipelines.
insights.quote: the factory knows which changes can pass on automated evidence and which require a person to decide.
insights.locator: Sonar frames approval as part of

insights.claim: Across Meta, PyTorch, OpenAI and Anthropic, the common pattern is scoped trust: approval gated on author trust and calibrated risk scores (Meta/PyTorch), change type (OpenAI), or what an action could break (Anthropic), with reverts and misses fed back into the system.
insights.speaker: Andrew Hoblitzell
insights.so_what: Auto-approval is becoming an industry norm; vendors of risk scoring, sandboxing and review agents stand to benefit.
insights.locator: The common thread is scoped trust
